name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
benefit: Rs 6,000 per year in 3 instalments of Rs 2,000, paid directly to the bank account.
steps: Visit the PM-KISAN portal or your nearest CSC/Common Service Centre.
Choose 'New Farmer Registration' and enter Aadhaar, state and mobile.
Fill land and bank details and submit.
Complete e-KYC (OTP or biometric) so instalments are released.
notes: Income-tax payers, government employees and pensioners earning Rs 10,000+/month are generally excluded.

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Crop Insurance)
benefit: Insurance cover against crop loss from drought, flood, pests and natural calamities at a low farmer premium (about 2% kharif, 1.5% rabi).
steps: Apply through your bank, CSC or the PMFBY portal before the cut-off date for the season.
Declare the crop and area sown.
Pay the farmer share of the premium.
Report crop loss within 72 hours through the crop insurance app, helpline or bank.
notes: Enrolment is season-wise; check cut-off dates for your district.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / NABARD
benefit: Short-term crop loans at subsidised interest (about 4% effective with prompt repayment) with a flexible credit limit.
steps: Visit your bank branch (cooperative, regional rural or commercial bank).
Ask for the KCC application form and fill it in.
Submit documents; the bank assesses your credit limit from land and crops.
Receive the card and use it for seeds, fertiliser and other farm inputs.
notes: Limits and interest subvention depend on the bank and the latest government notification.

name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (Health Insurance)
benefit: Cashless hospital treatment up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year at empanelled hospitals. Seniors aged 70+ are covered regardless of income.
documents: Ration card or proof of family entitlement
steps: Check eligibility on the PM-JAY portal ('Am I Eligible') or at an Ayushman Mitra desk in an empanelled hospital.
Complete e-KYC with Aadhaar to generate the Ayushman card.
Carry the card to an empanelled hospital for cashless treatment.
notes: Eligibility for most families is based on SECC deprivation data and state lists.

name: PM Awas Yojana - Gramin (Rural Housing)
benefit: Financial assistance of about Rs 1.2 lakh (plains) / Rs 1.3 lakh (hilly areas) to build a pucca house, plus convergence with MGNREGA wages and toilet support.
steps: Contact your Gram Panchayat / Block office to check if your name is on the PMAY-G permanent wait list.
Provide Aadhaar and bank details for verification.
After sanction, build in stages; instalments are released after geo-tagged photos at each stage.
notes: Beneficiaries are selected from the SECC/Awaas+ list through Gram Sabha.

name: PM Awas Yojana - Urban
benefit: Housing support and interest subsidy on home loans for urban families with income up to Rs 9 lakh per year (EWS/LIG/MIG).
documents: Proof that family does not own a pucca house
steps: Apply on the PMAY-Urban portal or via your Urban Local Body / bank.
Choose the component (beneficiary-led construction or credit-linked subsidy).
Submit documents and track the application online.
notes: Income slabs: EWS up to Rs 3 lakh, LIG Rs 3-6 lakh, MIG Rs 6-9 lakh. Check the latest guidelines.

name: PM Ujjwala Yojana (Free LPG Connection)
benefit: Free LPG connection for women from poor households, with a refill subsidy.
documents: BPL ration card or SECC proof
steps: Visit the nearest LPG distributor or apply on the PMUY portal.
Fill the KYC form and attach documents.
Distributor verifies and installs the connection.
notes: The household must not already have an LPG connection.

name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
benefit: High-interest small savings account for a girl child's education and marriage expenses, with tax benefits. The interest rate is revised every quarter.
documents: Parent/guardian Aadhaar and PAN or ID
steps: Visit any post office or authorised bank.
Fill the SSY account opening form with the birth certificate.
Deposit the minimum amount (Rs 250) and receive the passbook.
notes: Account must be opened before the girl turns 10; max two girls per family (exceptions apply).

name: PM Matru Vandana Yojana (Maternity Benefit)
benefit: Cash incentive of about Rs 5,000 for the first living child (more under the latest Mission Shakti norms), paid in instalments to support nutrition and rest.
steps: Register the pregnancy at your Anganwadi centre or health facility.
Fill the application form with the Anganwadi worker/ASHA.
Submit documents; instalments follow health check-ups and vaccination milestones.
notes: Government employees and those covered under similar maternity benefits are generally excluded.

name: Atal Pension Yojana
benefit: Guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 after age 60, depending on the contribution.
steps: Visit your bank branch or use net banking.
Fill the APY registration form and choose the pension amount.
Keep the monthly contribution auto-debited from your account.
notes: Income-tax payers are not eligible to join. Needs a bank account.

name: PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (Life Insurance)
benefit: Rs 2 lakh life insurance cover for a premium of about Rs 436 per year.
documents: Savings bank account with auto-debit consent
steps: Visit your bank branch or use net banking/mobile banking.
Give auto-debit consent for the annual premium.
Renew every year (auto-renewal available).
notes: Premium is subject to revision; check with your bank.

name: PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (Accident Insurance)
benefit: Rs 2 lakh cover for accidental death/full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, at about Rs 20 per year.
documents: Savings bank account with auto-debit consent
steps: Visit your bank or use net banking.
Give consent for the yearly premium auto-debit.
Renew yearly.
notes: Needs a bank account.

name: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (Zero-Balance Bank Account)
benefit: Zero-balance bank account with RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover and overdraft facility.
documents: Aadhaar card or other officially valid ID
steps: Visit any bank branch or Bank Mitra.
Fill the Jan Dhan account form with KYC documents.
Receive the passbook and RuPay card.
notes: Opening a bank account is also the first step to receive most direct benefit transfers.

name: PM MUDRA Yojana (Business Loan)
benefit: Collateral-free loans for small non-farm businesses: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishor (up to Rs 5 lakh), Tarun (up to Rs 10 lakh), with higher limits for Tarun Plus.
steps: Prepare a short business plan and cost estimate.
Apply at a bank, NBFC or MFI, or via the Udyamimitra portal.
Choose the right category (Shishu/Kishor/Tarun) and submit documents.
notes: For non-agricultural income-generating activities only.

name: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor Loan)
benefit: Collateral-free working-capital loan starting at Rs 10,000 for street vendors, with higher tranches on timely repayment and a digital-payment cashback incentive.
documents: Certificate of Vending / ID card or Letter of Recommendation from the urban local body
steps: Apply on the PM SVANidhi portal or at a CSC.
Upload your vending certificate or request a Letter of Recommendation from your municipality.
The lender sanctions the loan after verification.
notes: Vendors should have been operating on or before the cut-off date set in the scheme guidelines.

name: PM Vishwakarma (Artisans and Craftspeople)
benefit: Skill training with a stipend (about Rs 500/day), a toolkit incentive of Rs 15,000 and collateral-free loans up to Rs 3 lakh at a concessional rate.
steps: Register on the PM Vishwakarma portal through a CSC.
Complete biometric Aadhaar e-KYC.
Get verified by the Gram Panchayat/ULB and district committee.
Receive the PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card, then enrol for training and benefits.
notes: Covers 18 traditional trades such as carpenter, blacksmith, potter, tailor, weaver. Government employees' families are excluded.

name: MGNREGA (Rural Employment Guarantee)
benefit: Up to 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household each year.
steps: Apply at your Gram Panchayat for a Job Card.
Submit a written or oral request for work.
Receive work within 15 days or claim an unemployment allowance.
notes: Adult members willing to do unskilled manual work are eligible.

name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension (NSAP)
benefit: Monthly pension for elderly people from poor households. The central share is small and states usually add a top-up.
steps: Apply at your Gram Panchayat, Municipal office or e-Mitra/CSC.
Attach age and BPL proof.
After verification the pension is credited monthly to your bank account.
notes: State governments run their own old-age pension schemes with different rates; check your state's portal too.

name: e-Shram Card (Unorganised Workers)
benefit: Universal Account Number card for unorganised workers with Rs 2 lakh accident insurance and access to future social security benefits.
steps: Register for free on the e-Shram portal or at any CSC.
Verify with Aadhaar OTP and fill in occupation and bank details.
Download the e-Shram card.
notes: Not for EPFO/ESIC members or income-tax payers.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students
benefit: Tuition/fee reimbursement and maintenance allowance for Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10.
steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) for the current year.
Fill in the application and upload documents.
Get it verified by your institute and the nodal officer.
Track the status on NSP.
notes: Family income limit is as per the latest scholarship guidelines (about Rs 2.5 lakh).

name: Merit-cum-Means Scholarship for Minorities
benefit: Course-fee and maintenance support for minority-community students in professional and technical courses.
steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal.
Fill the application and upload documents.
Get it verified by the institute and nodal officer.
notes: Open to Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain and Parsi students; professional/technical courses at UG/PG level.

name: Central Sector Scholarship for College Students
benefit: Annual scholarship (about Rs 12,000 for graduation) for meritorious students from low-income families.
steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal.
Fill in the application with marks and income details.
Verification is done by the institute and the nodal officer.
notes: Usually requires being above the 80th percentile in Class 12 for your board and stream.

name: Mukhyamantri Ladli Behna Yojana (Madhya Pradesh)
benefit: Monthly financial assistance of about Rs 1,250 directly to eligible women.
steps: Visit your ward office, Gram Panchayat or Lok Seva Kendra.
Fill the application form with your Samagra ID.
After verification, payments are credited monthly.
notes: State schemes change often; confirm the amount and eligibility with the official portal.
